source:
Maya: Why did the outage last four hours? The failover never triggered. I watched the dashboard and the standby stayed idle the whole time.
Dev: The failover did trigger. It flipped at 02:14 and the standby came up, but its replica was six hours stale, so every request it served was wrong and we had to fail back.
Maya: If it flipped at 02:14 the standby would have taken traffic, and the traffic graph for the standby is flat until 06:00.
Dev: The traffic graph is flat because the health check rejected the stale replica and kept routing to the dead primary. The failover log has the 02:14 entry.
Maya: Then the fix is the failover trigger, not the replica.
Dev: The fix is replica freshness. A trigger that hands traffic to stale data is worse than no trigger.
Maya: We agree the four hours were unacceptable and that the runbook has to change before the next incident.
Dev: Agreed on that. What we disagree about is which piece failed.

extraction.mainQuestion: Why did the outage last four hours?

positions.label: The failover never triggered
positions.thesis: The outage lasted four hours because the failover never triggered and the standby stayed idle.
positions.steelman: The standby's traffic graph is flat for the whole window; a failover that had fired would have put traffic on it, so the trigger is the piece that failed.

groundingQuotes.quote: the standby stayed idle the whole time

positions.label: The failover fired onto a stale replica
positions.thesis: The outage lasted four hours because the failover did trigger but the standby's replica was six hours stale, forcing a fail-back.
positions.steelman: The failover log shows the 02:14 flip; the standby carried no traffic only because the health check rejected stale data, so replica freshness is the piece that failed.

groundingQuotes.quote: its replica was six hours stale

claims.statement: The failover log records a flip to the standby at 02:14.

resolution.condition: Read the failover log for a 02:14 entry and the standby health-check log for the same window.

groundingQuotes.quote: The failover log has the 02:14 entry.
I watched the dashboard and the standby stayed idle the whole time.

claims.statement: The standby's traffic graph is flat until 06:00.

resolution.condition: Check whether the health check rejected the standby during the window, which would explain a flat graph after a real flip.

groundingQuotes.quote: the traffic graph for the standby is flat until 06:00
The traffic graph is flat because the health check rejected the stale replica

commonGroundCandidates.statement: The four-hour outage was unacceptable and the runbook must change before the next incident.

groundingQuotes.quote: We agree the four hours were unacceptable

disagreementCandidates.question: Did the failover trigger at 02:14?
disagreementCandidates.summary: Maya reads the flat standby traffic as proof the failover never fired; Dev says the log shows a 02:14 flip and the health check kept traffic off the stale standby.

participantStances.stance: No; the standby stayed idle all night.
Yes; the log has the 02:14 entry and the health check explains the flat graph.

disagreementCandidates.resolutionCondition: Reconcile the failover log with the standby health-check log for 02:14 to 06:00.

caveats: The main question is phrased as a why-question; both speakers accept that the outage lasted four hours.
